pages.quiz:
GEOGRAPHY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: GEOGRAPHY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which statement about Water Cycle and Action of Rivers is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Treat Water Cycle and Action of Rivers as rumours only.
   B. Say Water Cycle and Action of Rivers never happens in Kenya.
   C. Skip evidence when discussing Water Cycle and Action of Rivers.
   D. Explain Water Cycle and Action of Rivers with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

2. Which statement about Map Reading and Interpretation is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Map Reading and Interpretation.
   B. Say Map Reading and Interpretation never happens in Kenya.
   C. Treat Map Reading and Interpretation as rumours only.
   D. Explain Map Reading and Interpretation with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

3. Which statement about Weather is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Weather.
   B. Explain Weather with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Treat Weather as rumours only.
   D. Say Weather never happens in Kenya.

4. Which statement about Soils is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Treat Soils as rumours only.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Soils.
   C. Say Soils never happens in Kenya.
   D. Explain Soils with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

5. Kenya’s capital city is: (1 mark)
   A. Nairobi
   B. Kisumu
   C. Nakuru
   D. Mombasa

6. A map key (legend) is used to: (1 mark)
   A. Explain symbols used on a map
   B. Measure rainfall only
   C. Replace the compass rose
   D. Name the president

7. Which statement about Mass Wasting is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Mass Wasting never happens in Kenya.
   B. Treat Mass Wasting as rumours only.
   C. Explain Mass Wasting with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Mass Wasting.

8. Which statement about Vegetation is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Vegetation with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Treat Vegetation as rumours only.
   C. Say Vegetation never happens in Kenya.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Vegetation.

9. Which statement about Statistical Methods is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Statistical Methods with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Treat Statistical Methods as rumours only.
   C. Say Statistical Methods never happens in Kenya.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Statistical Methods.

10. Citizenship responsibility includes: (1 mark)
   A. Obeying laws and caring for public property
   B. Destroying road signs
   C. Avoiding all community work
   D. Littering in markets

11. Which statement about Elementary Surveying is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Elementary Surveying with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Elementary Surveying.
   C. Treat Elementary Surveying as rumours only.
   D. Say Elementary Surveying never happens in Kenya.

12. Which statement about Geographic Information Systems is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Geographic Information Systems.
   B. Explain Geographic Information Systems with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Treat Geographic Information Systems as rumours only.
   D. Say Geographic Information Systems never happens in Kenya.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Water Cycle and Action of Rivers and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Agriculture - Wheat in Kenya and Russia - Maize in Kenya and Mexico, - Coffee in and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Wildlife and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Tourism and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

====

1. D — Explain Water Cycle and Action of Rivers with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

2. D — Explain Map Reading and Interpretation with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

3. B — Explain Weather with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

4. D — Explain Soils with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

5. A — Nairobi

6. A — Explain symbols used on a map

7. C — Explain Mass Wasting with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

8. A — Explain Vegetation with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

9. A — Explain Statistical Methods with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

10. A — Obeying laws and caring for public property

11. A — Explain Elementary Surveying with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

12. B — Explain Geographic Information Systems with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Water Cycle and Action of Rivers; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Agriculture - Wheat in Kenya and Russia - Maize in Kenya and Mexico, - Coffee in; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Wildlife; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Tourism; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
